clue.text: Ruddy brilliant athlete — one to train on the pole in garden

definitions.text: one to train on the pole in garden

parts.note: a ruddy, brilliant colour is scarlet, a bright vivid red
a runner is a track athlete

explanation.surface: A red-faced star of the track is somehow also something a gardener ties to a pole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruddy brilliant athlete' reads as praise for a red-cheeked sprinter; it splits into a bright red colour and a track athlete, and the rest is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This climbing bean is grown up canes or poles in British vegetable gardens and trained to twine around them.

clue.text: My poor clue not superior? Dreadful material!

indicators.note: dreadful says the remaining letters are in a terrible, jumbled state and must be rearranged
not tells us to leave out the letter standing for superior from the clue words

parts.note: U is the old abbreviation for upper-class, socially superior, as in U and non-U

explanation.surface: A setter mocks their own feeble clue as dreadful stuff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not superior' drops the U from MY POOR CLUE, leaving MYPOORCLE, which 'Dreadful' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A copolymer is a plastic or similar substance made by polymerising two different monomers together, so it is a material.

clue.text: Out of practice in game, starts to seem tired, yawning

parts.note: RU stands for rugby union, the game

indicators.note: starts to picks the opening letter of each of the next three words

explanation.surface: A player who has not trained looks tired and yawns during the match.
explanation.walkthrough: RU (rugby union) is followed by the first letters of 'seem tired, yawning', which the phrase 'starts to' selects.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone whose skills have faded from lack of use is said to be rusty, like neglected metal.

clue.text: Attractive net, fanciful sort of decoration

indicators.note: fanciful suggests the letters of net are rearranged imaginatively

parts.note: icing is the sugary decoration put on a cake

explanation.surface: Someone admires a pretty net and some ornate cake decoration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'net' looks like part of the description of something attractive; 'fanciful' is the anagram signal working on it alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Something enticing tempts or lures you, which is to say it is alluring and appealing.

clue.text: Begrudge being on repeat mission?

definitions.meaning: to begrudge something is to feel bitter or aggrieved about it
someone dispatched a second time has been sent again, written with the prefix re-

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles about being sent out on the same errand once more.
explanation.definitionFit: To feel aggrieved at something is the verb's usual sense, while the hyphenated reading means dispatched once more.

clue.text: Island not having old money

parts.note: something that is not old is new
the guinea was a British gold coin, later a sum of 21 shillings, now old money

explanation.surface: An islander complains of having no ancient coins.
explanation.walkthrough: A GUINEA was a pre-decimal British coin worth 21 shillings; a newly minted one would be the opposite of old money.
explanation.definitionFit: This large Pacific landmass north of Australia is the world's second-largest island.

clue.text: Story about Conservative being on the up brings applause

indicators.note: in a down clue, being on the up says the built letters are read from the bottom upwards
about says the story word goes around the abbreviation for Conservative

parts.note: a tale is a story

explanation.surface: A story about a Tory on the rise wins applause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts C inside TALE to make TALCE, and 'being on the up' turns that round in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Eclat is brilliant success or acclaim, the kind of public approval that brings cheering.

clue.text: Dog who might have engaged in action near the tweed?

definitions.meaning: a breed of small rough-coated terrier

definitions.text: who might have engaged in action near the tweed?
definitions.meaning: a terrier is slang for a Territorial Army soldier, and the River Tweed marks the border between England and Scotland, so a Territorial fighting there

explanation.surface: A dog is pictured as having fought along the River Tweed.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tweed is the river forming part of the England-Scotland border; 'terrier' is British slang for a part-time Territorial Army soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: The breed takes its name from the Cheviot Hills region on the Anglo-Scottish frontier, where it was used for hunting foxes.

clue.text: With these you may see what's needed for a romantic champagne dinner

definitions.text: what's needed for a romantic champagne dinner
definitions.meaning: two drinking vessels, one for each diner, to hold the champagne

explanation.surface: A couple prepare for an intimate evening with bubbly and maybe their specs.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both spectacles for sight and a couple of drinking vessels for a dinner for two.

clue.text: River going this way and that to places hot and cold?

indicators.note: going this way and that means the river's name is written once backwards and once forwards

parts.note: the Po is the great river of northern Italy
the Po again, this time read forwards
sites are places

explanation.surface: A river meanders to and fro between hot and cold spots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going this way and that' means the one river is written twice, backwards then forwards; the definition is an example, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot and cold are a classic pair of contrary words, each the antonym of the other.

clue.text: Girl's energy of intention reduced by mum

definitions.note: the definition with its 's reads as girl is, linking to the wordplay

indicators.note: reduced says the word is cut short by losing its final letter

parts.note: will is the force of determination behind what one intends
ma is a familiar word for mother

explanation.surface: A girl's drive is curbed by her mother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced' drops the final letter of the willpower word; 'Girl's' is the definition plus a linking 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Wilma is a female first name, so it fits a girl.

clue.text: A special sheep that's loved by little girl?

definitions.meaning: the famous ewe that was the first mammal cloned from an adult cell, in Scotland in 1996
a child's toy figure of a person, cuddled by small girls

explanation.surface: A little girl dotes on an unusual sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs to the cloned ewe, and the same word is the nursery term for a toy doll.

clue.text: Musician badly cut, nipped by bird

indicators.note: nipped by says the bird's beak closes around the scrambled letters

parts.note: the condor is a huge vulture of the Americas

indicators.note: badly says the letters of cut are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A musician has been savaged by a bird and is bleeding.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a wounded musician, but 'badly' is the anagram signal and 'nipped by' means held inside the bird's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The person who directs an orchestra is a musician leading the performance with a baton.

clue.text: Strange noise keeps one dancing

parts.note: rum is a British informal word for odd or strange

indicators.note: keeps says the noise word holds the numeral one inside it

parts.note: a bang is a loud noise
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An odd sound persists while someone dances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strange' is the British slang 'rum', not an anagram signal; 'keeps' means the noise word holds the Roman numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: Performing the Cuban ballroom dance in question is a form of dancing.

clue.text: Like maths that involves some unknown characters

definitions.text: Like maths that involves some unknown characters

parts.words: Like maths that involves some unknown characters
parts.note: describes the branch of mathematics where letters such as x and y stand for unknown quantities; characters suggests mysterious people

explanation.definitionFit: Equations in this branch of mathematics use letters as symbols for unknown values.

clue.text: University fine for housing agreeable international agency

indicators.note: housing says the first pair of letters enclose the next piece

parts.note: F stands for fine, as on pencil leads
nice means agreeable

explanation.surface: A university's penalty pays for lodging a pleasant global body.
explanation.walkthrough: U and F, from 'University fine', are split by NICE, which 'housing' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: The United Nations Children's Fund is a worldwide body, an agency of the UN.

clue.text: Tea bar about to open for a coach

indicators.note: to open for says the a comes at the front, starting off the following piece

parts.note: char is British slang for tea
to ban is to bar
C stands for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A tea bar is about to open for a coach party.
explanation.walkthrough: CHAR is British slang for tea; A opens BAN plus C (circa, about).
explanation.definitionFit: A charabanc is an old open-topped motor coach used for day trips and outings.

clue.text: Support team that's bottom

parts.note: to back is to support
a side is a team

explanation.surface: A supporting team is languishing at the foot of the league.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottom' looks like a league position, but it is the definition: the body part.
explanation.definitionFit: The rump or buttocks one sits on is a bottom.

clue.text: Composer in a spin, for example, about to show anger

indicators.note: in a spin says the composer's name is turned right round

parts.note: Thomas Arne was the English composer of Rule, Britannia!

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so the two letters go backwards

parts.note: eg abbreviates exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: A composer flies into a rage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a spin' turns ARNE into ENRA and 'about' turns EG into GE.
explanation.definitionFit: To make someone furious, or to fly into a fury, is to display rage; the verb fits the definition.

clue.text: In big building an expert enjoyed himself

indicators.note: In says the following words go inside the large building

parts.note: a hall is a large building
a dab, as in dab hand, is an expert

explanation.surface: An expert had a fine time in a large building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dab hand' is British for an expert, so a dab alone means one; 'In' puts that inside the big building.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means had a thoroughly good time, like someone at a party.

clue.text: Blade specially tooled

indicators.note: specially suggests letters arranged in a special new order

explanation.surface: A blade has been crafted with care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'specially' rearranges TOOLED.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish city was famous for its swords, so a Toledo is a fine sword.

clue.text: Barrier constructed by police could be black door

indicators.note: could be says the letters of black door may become something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: A police barrier might look like a dark front door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges BLACK DOOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Officers set up an obstruction across a highway to stop vehicles.

clue.text: Some man to name here

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A request to name a man from the clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition 'here' cannot replace a man's name; the whole clue defines it: a man's name is concealed here, in 'man to name'.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue asks for a man's name concealed within it, and this is a male first name.

clue.text: Boldness needed to make money

definitions.meaning: cheek or nerve, as in having the ... neck to do something

explanation.surface: Nerve is what it takes to get rich.
explanation.definitionFit: Impudence and cash are both senses of the slang word, common in northern England.

clue.text: Cheese flan three-quarters gone — not lasting long

parts.note: brie is a soft French cheese

indicators.note: three-quarters gone leaves only the first of the four letters of flan

explanation.surface: Cheese and a flan, mostly eaten, do not last long.
explanation.walkthrough: 'three-quarters gone' keeps only F from the four-letter FLAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Something brief is short-lived, of little duration.

clue.text: Artist by way out — one going with "bye"?

indicators.note: by means beside, so the artist comes next
going says the numeral for one departs from the word for way out

parts.note: an exit is a way out
I is the Roman numeral for one
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: An artist takes the exit, waving goodbye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one going' removes I from EXIT; RA (Royal Academician) goes 'by' it. A bye in cricket is a run scored without the batsman hitting the ball, counted among the extras.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, byes are runs not credited to a batsman and are classed with wides and no-balls as sundries.

clue.text: Get rid of priest in team that's going wrong

parts.note: Eli was the priest who raised Samuel in the Bible

indicators.note: going wrong says the letters of in team are put in disorder

explanation.surface: A team plotting to remove its priest is losing badly.
explanation.walkthrough: ELI is the biblical priest; 'going wrong' rearranges IN TEAM.
explanation.definitionFit: To eliminate is to remove or knock out, as a team is knocked out of a cup.

clue.text: A scrum? Consequence of what has happened earlier

definitions.meaning: in rugby a knock-on, dropping the ball forwards, is penalised by a scrum, so a scrum is its result

definitions.text: Consequence of what has happened earlier
definitions.meaning: a secondary result flowing from an earlier event

explanation.surface: A rugby set piece is described as the result of earlier events.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means an indirect result; in rugby a scrum follows from the infringement of the same name.
